simple_definition: The price a memory maker and a big buyer agree privately for a month or a quarter; most memory is sold this way.
technical_definition: Negotiated price for DRAM/NAND sold to OEMs, hyperscalers and module makers, historically reset monthly or quarterly; not published, so research firms (e.g. DRAMeXchange) estimate it from surveys and report session high/low/average.

simple_definition: The price of memory chips traded day to day between brokers, module makers and distributors outside long contracts; it reacts first when shortages or gluts appear.
technical_definition: Price in the small open/spot market (vendors, OEMs/system integrators, channel distributors, module makers, brokers); above contract prices in shortages and below them when sellers dump inventory; DRAMeXchange updates it three times daily.

simple_definition: A contract where the buyer must pay for an agreed amount even if it ends up taking less.
technical_definition: Binding volume commitment; used in Micron's 2026 Strategic Customer Agreements and other multi-year memory LTAs, often with prepayments and price floors/ceilings.

simple_definition: Micron's name for its 2026 multi-year memory supply deals in which customers commit to buy set amounts, often paying cash up front.
technical_definition: Take-or-pay agreements (5 years for data-center/consumer, 3 years for automotive) with fixed prices or min/max price bands and customer deposits; 16 signed by June 2026 covering ~20% of Micron DRAM and ~1/3 of NAND volume.

simple_definition: Total sales divided by the number of units (or bits) sold; for memory it is the main measure of price moves.
technical_definition: Memory makers report ASP changes per gigabit (bit ASP); Micron states annual DRAM ASP changes ranged roughly +40% to -40% or worse over five years.

simple_definition: How much memory capacity (counted in bits) a company ships; memory revenue equals bit shipments times price per bit.
technical_definition: Memory volume measure (Gb or GB equivalents); bit supply growth guidance is the main supply-discipline signal (e.g. Micron guided negative DRAM bit supply growth for CY2023).

simple_definition: The number of new silicon wafers a factory puts into production; cutting them is how chipmakers reduce output.
technical_definition: Fab input measure (wafers per month); Micron cut DRAM/NAND wafer starts ~20% (Nov 2022) and Kioxia ~30% (Oct 2022) in the downturn.

simple_definition: An accounting loss taken when chips in stock are worth less than they cost to make.
technical_definition: Under GAAP, inventory is carried at the lower of cost or net realizable value; when memory prices fall below cost, makers record write-downs (Micron US$1.43bn in FQ2 2023).

simple_definition: An import tax a country charges to offset a foreign government's subsidy to the exporter.
technical_definition: Duty set equal to the net subsidy rate found by the investigating authority; the US imposed 44.29% on Hynix DRAMs in 2003 after finding state-directed creditor support.

simple_definition: An agreement where an exporting country limits its own exports, usually under pressure, which tends to raise prices.
technical_definition: Irwin describes MITI's post-1986 output/export cuts as an 'antidumping' VER aimed at a price target, which raised DRAM prices and profits of Japanese producers.

simple_definition: A message from a chipmaker telling customers it will stop making a product and when last orders are due.
technical_definition: Micron's June 2025 EOL notices for DDR4/LPDDR4 preceded sharp DDR4 price rises as supply shifted to DDR5/HBM.
